name: Create Shape-Provider Goal (shape-provider-goal-creation)
description: Activity-driven implementation of shape-provider goal creation per OpenSpec change 2026-04-26-shape-provider-goal-creation §3. When a missing input shape cannot be bound by pool selection or in-scope producer selection, this activity composes a NEW goal-shaped impulse whose `endpoint_output_shapes: [target_shape]` constraint will route the dispatched activity to a producer of that shape via the existing variant-selection pipe (goal-processing-activity-driven). Five signal-gathering tasks (forward-chain producers, prior paths with terminal-shape match, concept-db related concepts, impulse co-occurrence ranking, cost/risk priors) accumulate evidence; the parent-chain lookup task surfaces the parent execution's composition_chain for cycle detection; a final LLM compose_goal task ingests all signals and emits a single goal-shaped impulse. Three recursion-safety guards (depth, cycle, budget) are embedded in the compose_goal LLM prompt and surface as `human_in_the_loop_required: true` plus a `failure_mode` per the validators-and-failure-modes taxonomy. The activity itself records traces for Thompson Sampling — variants (cost-optimized, concept-omitted, etc.) emerge from the learning loop via save-as-variant.

variables.name: target_shape
variables.description: The missing impulse shape that the emitted sub-goal must produce. Becomes `endpoint_output_shapes: [target_shape]` on the goal-shaped output impulse, which the downstream variant-selection step uses as a hard constraint when picking a dispatched activity.

variables.name: parent_goal_text
variables.description: The parent goal's human-readable text. Provides semantic context to the LLM composer so the sub-goal text references the ancestor intent (e.g. 'as part of <parent>, produce <shape>' rather than just 'produce <shape>').

variables.name: available_shapes
variables.description: Shapes already bound in the parent's impulse pool. Feeds the impulse_cooccurrence task — which of these historically co-occur as inputs to producers of `target_shape`? — so the composed goal text can hint at which existing impulses to surface to the sub-goal's producer.

variables.name: parent_execution_id
variables.description: Execution id of the parent activity whose missing-shape signal triggered this sub-goal. Used by the parent_chain_lookup task to resolve the parent's `composition_chain` (denormalized ancestor chain, root-first; see CLAUDE.md §Execution Trace Model) for cycle detection. When omitted (e.g. top-level invocations from the workbench), cycle detection short-circuits to 'no cycle possible' and the depth guard alone gates recursion.

variables.name: parent_depth
variables.description: Recursion depth of the parent. The emitted goal sets `depth: parent_depth + 1`. The depth guard in compose_goal sets `human_in_the_loop_required: true` AND `failure_mode.type: 'safety_breach'` (breach_type='depth') when `(parent_depth + 1) > max_recursion_depth`.

variables.name: remaining_budget_usd
variables.description: USD budget remaining for the parent's overall execution. The budget guard in compose_goal sets `human_in_the_loop_required: true` AND `failure_mode.type: 'budget_exhausted'` when the cheapest known producer's `avg_cost_usd` (signal 5) exceeds `remaining_budget_usd / 2` — heuristic 'leave headroom for parent's other tasks'. When omitted, budget guard is disabled.

variables.name: max_recursion_depth
variables.description: Hard ceiling on `depth`. Default 3 matches the design.md guard (`max_depth_default`). Configurable via this variable so org policies can tighten or loosen the bound; raising it should be a deliberate decision visible in the dispatch call.

tasks.description: Signal 1 — query the Thompson-Sampling backend for activities that produce `target_shape`.

config._target_shape_note: target_shape (variable) is not directly forwarded to the backend recommend route as a `required_shapes` filter — that filter wiring is part of the spec's discover-by-shapes mode but the recommend route uses a goal-enrichment-shaped impulse to derive expected_output_shapes server-side. The downstream variant_selection step in goal-processing-activity-driven applies the shape filter on the client side (Investigation #5 fix, 2026-04-22). Future cleanup: register a `discover_by_shapes` resolver that forwards `required_shapes: [target_shape]` directly. Until then, callers of this template can rely on the cost_risk_priors task to retrieve metrics for whichever candidates come back, and compose_goal to filter by output_shape compatibility in the final synthesis.

tasks.notes: Uses `activity_recommendation` (registered template-dispatchable resolver) which wraps `POST /v2/activities/recommend`. SIMPLIFICATION (per spec pragmatic-decisions allowance): the spec calls for `discover-by-shapes` mode=forward with `required_shapes: [target_shape]` filter, but `activity_recommendation` is the existing template-dispatchable wrapper around the recommendation+Thompson path — `discover_by_shapes` has no template-dispatchable resolver wrapper today (`producer_selection` calls discover-by-shapes too but with mode=candidates_with_scores + missingShape, which gives the same set of producers with composition scores). The downstream cost_risk_priors task (signal 5) reads `activityMetrics` for the candidates returned here, and compose_goal can choose to proceed or escalate based on the candidates' confidence. When the backend is unreachable, the resolver emits an empty `activity_recommendations` impulse (metadata.empty=true) — the chain still completes; compose_goal then leans on signals 2-4 and the LLM to draft a more verbose goal text.

tasks.description: Signal 2 — query existing `goal_execution_paths` whose `endpoint_output_shapes` contains `target_shape` (the new denormalized field landed in migration 092 / spec sibling §1).
tasks.notes: LIMITATION: `goalExecutionPath` is NOT one of activity-api's advertised impulse shapes (see `repos/metabob-activity-api/src/config.ts:158-189`); the `/v2/goal-paths` REST endpoint exists but cannot be reached via the `impulse-resolve` template-dispatchable path. SIMPLIFICATION (per spec pragmatic-decisions allowance): we attempt the read via `impulse-resolve` with pointer.type='goalExecutionPath' so the chain is well-formed for the future when activity-api adds the case. Until then this task gracefully returns an error/empty content, which compose_goal handles defensively — empty signal 2 just means 'no prior path closed this shape gap; lean harder on signals 1/3/4'. Filter parameters (`endpoint_output_shape: target_shape`) are forwarded as pointer fields for forward compatibility.

tasks.description: Signal 3 — query concept-db for concepts related to `target_shape`.
tasks.notes: LIMITATION: concept-db's `relatedConcepts` shape requires `pointer.concept_id` (a specific concept's id) — there is no `relatedConcepts-by-shape-name` endpoint; you'd need to resolve target_shape to a concept_id first (e.g. via concept-db's search route, which is not exposed as an advertised impulse shape). SIMPLIFICATION (per spec pragmatic-decisions allowance): we issue the resolve with `concept_id: target_shape` as a best-effort lookup — concept-db treats unknown ids gracefully (returns 404 / empty) and the chain continues. The compose_goal task treats an empty/error response as 'no concept context available' — not a failure. Future fix: register a concept-search-by-name shape (e.g. `conceptSearch` with `pointer.shape_name`) and route through that instead. The signal is enrichment for the LLM composer, not a hard requirement; signals 1+2+4+5 carry the load when 3 is empty.

config._producer_ids_note: Spec §3.5 calls for consuming producer ids from forward_chain_producers and `available_shapes`. The resolver's contract today consumes a trace array, not producer ids — producer ids are an upstream signal that would be used when fetching the relevant traces. The producer ids and available_shapes are wired into the compose_goal prompt via {{impulse:forward_chain_producers_result}} and {{available_shapes}}; the LLM cross-references them with signal 4's matrix when present.
config._available_shapes_note: available_shapes is forwarded to the LLM composer via {{available_shapes}}, not to this resolver, because the resolver's input shape is a trace array. See description for the future-fix path.

tasks.notes: Identifies which of the parent's `available_shapes` historically co-occur as inputs to producers of `target_shape`. The resolver is deterministic and stateless (see ImpulseCooccurrenceResolver) — given execution traces it pair-counts same-task co-occurrence of impulse signatures. SIMPLIFICATION: the resolver expects traces on `config.traces` or as a JSON-serialised input impulse; it does NOT itself fetch traces from the backend. Without an upstream task that fetches `executionTraceWithSignatures` keyed by target_shape, this resolver runs over an empty trace set and emits an empty cooccurrence matrix — that's a structurally-valid no-op which compose_goal handles defensively (empty signal 4 = no cooccurrence hint; LLM composer relies on signals 1/2/3/5 + parent_goal_text). Future fix: prepend a task that calls `impulse-resolve` with `pointer.type='executionTraceWithSignatures'` filtered by activity output_shape=target_shape, then feed the result here as an input impulse. Out of scope per spec §3.5 which only requires producer ids + available_shapes (we forward both via config so a future refactor can wire trace fetching in without changing this template's signal-output contract).

tasks.description: Signal 5a — fetch `activityMetrics` for the producer candidates from signal 1.
tasks.notes: The pointer requires `activityId` (singular) per `activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts:852-883`; SIMPLIFICATION (per spec pragmatic-decisions allowance and infra gap B 'no foreach over arrays'): we issue ONE metrics resolve at the top of the cost stream and let the compose_goal LLM cross-reference per-candidate `avg_cost_usd` it sees in `forward_chain_producers_result` (the recommend route returns `metrics.confidence`, `metrics.success_rate`, etc. inline). When a future foreach primitive lands, expand this into a per-candidate metrics fetch. The hardcoded `activityId: 'unknown'` is a deliberate no-op anchor — the compose_goal prompt reads cost from `forward_chain_producers_result` instead and treats this task's output as a structural placeholder. Documents the spec intent without fabricating an arbitrary candidate id.

tasks.description: Signal 5b — fetch `toolRiskProfile` for the producer candidates from signal 1.
tasks.notes: PARALLEL to cost_priors (both depend on forward_chain_producers, neither depends on the other; the executor schedules them concurrently). The pointer accepts an optional `activityId` filter; when omitted, the route returns aggregated tool risk across the org. We send the unfiltered query — compose_goal cross-references with `forward_chain_producers_result` to spot high-risk tools per candidate. Same SIMPLIFICATION rationale as cost_priors: per-candidate per-tool fetching awaits a foreach primitive; meanwhile aggregated risk is a sufficient first-cut signal for compose_goal's heuristic 'any candidate carries destructive ops?' check.

tasks.description: Cycle-detection precursor — fetch the parent execution's `composition_chain` (denormalized ancestor chain, root-first; see CLAUDE.md §Execution Trace Model).
tasks.notes: The compose_goal task uses this chain to enforce the cycle guard (spec §3.9): if any ancestor's `endpoint_output_shapes` contains `target_shape`, that ancestor is already trying to produce the shape and recursing would be redundant, so the goal is emitted with `human_in_the_loop_required: true` and `failure_mode.type: 'safety_breach'` (breach_type='cycle'). When `parent_execution_id` is empty (top-level invocations), the cycle guard short-circuits to 'no cycle possible' and the depth guard alone gates recursion. This task uses `impulse-resolve` with pointer.type='activityExecutionTrace'; the route requires `executionId` (see `repos/metabob-activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts:719-724`) and returns 400 when omitted, so the lookup is best-effort: if `parent_execution_id` is empty/missing the resolver returns an error which compose_goal interprets as 'no parent chain available, cycle check skipped'.

tasks.description: Final task — LLM composes the goal-shaped output impulse from all five signals plus the parent-chain context.
tasks.notes: The prompt enforces ALL THREE recursion-safety guards (depth, cycle, budget) inline because the existing template format does NOT support per-task validation rules that conditionally rewrite output fields, and expressing each guard as a separate task with its own conditional would multiply the dispatched-activity count for no behavioral gain. CHOICE: guards in the LLM prompt is the simplification documented in metadata.openQuestions. When a deterministic guard-evaluator resolver lands (or per-task validation rules with mutable output schema), the prompt-embedded guards can be lifted out without changing this template's external contract (the goal impulse it emits). The prompt outputs a single JSON object matching the goal-shape schema in design.md §Goal-as-shape-producer framing; the LLM is instructed to be defensive about empty/error signal inputs (signals 2-4 may be empty; signal 5a/5b may be aggregated rather than per-candidate).

metadata.author: shape-provider-goal-creation
openQuestions: Validation-rule mechanism (spec §3.8-§3.10): the existing template format has no per-task validation rules that conditionally REWRITE output fields (it has `task.validation` for required files / forbidden patterns, but those reject the task; they don't transform the output JSON). Expressing each guard as a separate task with a `conditional` would split emission across multiple tasks and require a final merge step, which has no template-format primitive either. CHOICE made here: embed all three guards (depth, cycle, budget) in the compose_goal LLM prompt, since the LLM already has access to all the inputs the guards need (parent_depth, max_recursion_depth, parent_chain_lookup_result, remaining_budget_usd, signal 5 cost data). The LLM is instructed to be deterministic about the guard logic — the prompt enumerates the exact conditions and the exact failure_mode shapes per migration 091. FUTURE FIX: when a deterministic guard-evaluator resolver lands (e.g. `goal_guard_evaluator` taking depth/budget/chain inputs and emitting a guard_result impulse), the LLM prompt-embedded guards can be lifted out without changing this template's external contract (the goal-shape impulse it emits).

discover-by-shapes resolver: spec §3.2 calls for `activity_recommendation` OR `producer_selection` with selectionMethod='deterministic' to query producers for target_shape. We use `activity_recommendation` because it's the more direct wrapper around the recommend+Thompson path; `producer_selection` is geared for slot-binding-style 'pick one to dispatch now' rather than 'enumerate candidates with metrics'. The forward-chain task does NOT pass target_shape as a `required_shapes` filter to the backend — the recommend route derives expected_output_shapes from the goal_enrichment-shaped input impulse server-side (see Investigation #5 fix in goal-processing-activity-driven). The downstream variant_selection step in the goal-processing chain applies output_shape compatibility on the client side. Future cleanup: register a `discover_by_shapes` resolver that forwards `required_shapes: [target_shape]` directly so this template can call it explicitly.

goalExecutionPath shape advertisement: spec §3.3 calls for an `impulse-resolve` to activity-api with `pointer.type='goalExecutionPath'` filtered by endpoint_output_shape=target_shape (the new field from sibling §1, migration 092). LIMITATION: `goalExecutionPath` is NOT in `repos/metabob-activity-api/src/config.ts:158-189` (advertised shapes). The case isn't yet wired in `repos/metabob-activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts`. This template's signal 2 task issues the resolve regardless so the chain is well-formed for the future when activity-api adds the case; meanwhile the resolver returns an error/empty content which compose_goal handles defensively. Follow-up: add `goalExecutionPath` to `config.ts` advertised shapes and a case in `routes/impulses.ts` that queries `goal_execution_paths` filtered by `endpoint_output_shapes CONTAINS $shape`.

concept-db relatedConcepts pointer: spec §3.4 calls for keying the lookup on `target_shape`. LIMITATION: concept-db's `relatedConcepts` shape requires `pointer.concept_id` (a specific concept's id), not a shape-name. There is no `relatedConcepts-by-shape-name` endpoint; resolving target_shape to a concept_id would require a separate concept-search call which isn't exposed as an advertised impulse shape. This template issues the resolve with `concept_id: target_shape` as a best-effort lookup — concept-db treats unknown ids gracefully (404 / empty), and compose_goal handles the error path. Follow-up: register a `conceptSearch` shape on concept-db with `pointer.shape_name`, OR have concept-db's relatedConcepts case accept either concept_id or shape_name with a documented precedence.

impulse_cooccurrence trace fetching: spec §3.5 says 'config consumes producer ids from task 1 and available_shapes'. The `impulse_cooccurrence` resolver's actual contract is a trace array (inline `config.traces` or via input impulse parsing); it does NOT fetch traces from the backend. Without an upstream trace-fetching task, signal 4 runs over an empty trace set and emits an empty matrix. This is a structurally-valid no-op which compose_goal handles defensively. Follow-up: prepend a task that calls `impulse-resolve` with `pointer.type='executionTraceWithSignatures'` filtered by activity output_shape=target_shape, then pass the result as an input impulse to the cooccurrence task. Out of scope per the spec's strict 'producer ids + available_shapes' framing; producer ids are visible to compose_goal via the forward_chain_producers_result impulse and used in the LLM's reasoning regardless.

Per-candidate cost/risk fetching (spec §3.6): the spec calls for two parallel `vessel_resolve_call`s keyed on producer ids from signal 1. The pointers (activityMetrics requires activityId; toolRiskProfile accepts optional activityId) require ONE id per resolve, but the template format has no foreach/map primitive (infra gap B). SIMPLIFICATION: cost_priors anchors with a placeholder activityId='unknown' (resolver returns 404, treated as empty by compose_goal); risk_priors uses the unfiltered route which returns aggregated risk across the org. compose_goal cross-references the candidates' inline metrics from forward_chain_producers_result (the recommend route returns metrics.confidence, success_rate per candidate inline) for the cheapest-producer cost calculation. Follow-up: when foreach lands, expand into a per-candidate metrics+risk fetch.

Cycle-detection ancestor inspection: spec §3.9 says 'for each ancestor execution, read its goal-shaped output impulse'. The current parent_chain_lookup task fetches the immediate parent's full trace (which includes composition_chain — the ancestor list) but does NOT recursively fetch each ancestor's full trace + their goal impulses. SIMPLIFICATION: the compose_goal LLM is instructed to inspect whatever output_impulse shape data is present in the parent's trace (which embeds its own task outputs); for deeper-than-1 ancestor inspection it would need a multi-hop trace fetch which is N+1 problematic without a batch-resolve primitive. Conservative behaviour: when the immediate parent's output_impulses include target_shape, GUARD 2 trips. Multi-hop ancestor inspection is a follow-up; in practice depth>1 cycles are rare because the depth guard kicks in first (default max_recursion_depth=3).

failure_mode taxonomy alignment: the inline guards emit failure_mode objects matching migration 091 (failure_mode_taxonomy). When that migration's discriminated-union shape evolves, this template's compose_goal prompt MUST be updated to match — there's no schema validation on the LLM-emitted JSON beyond the structural shape implied by the prompt. Cross-spec coupling is documented in the design.md (this change is a consumer/emitter of validators-and-failure-modes' failure_mode shape).

Auto-dispatch vs human-only-dispatch policy (design.md §Cascade integration): this template emits the goal with `human_in_the_loop_required` populated by the guards. The DISPATCH policy (auto vs human-mediated) lives in the sibling impulse-binding-selection-layer's slot-binding meta-activity, not here. This template is a pure emitter; it does not call back into the dispatcher. The default in the design is human-only dispatch with auto-dispatch reserved for goals where `human_in_the_loop_required: false AND confidence_top_producer > 0.8 AND depth == 1`.
limitations: Validation rules embedded in compose_goal LLM prompt rather than as standalone task validations — see openQuestions[0]. Guard logic lives in the prompt; the LLM applies depth/cycle/budget checks deterministically.
Forward-chain producers task uses activity_recommendation rather than a target_shape-filtered discover-by-shapes call — see openQuestions[1]. Shape filtering happens client-side downstream.

Signal 2 (prior_paths_with_endpoint) issues an impulse-resolve to a shape (`goalExecutionPath`) that is not yet advertised by activity-api — see openQuestions[2]. Best-effort lookup; compose_goal handles empty/error responses.
Signal 3 (concept_lookup) keys relatedConcepts on target_shape as a concept_id — see openQuestions[3]. Best-effort; falls back gracefully when target_shape is not a known concept_id.
Signal 4 (cooccurrence_signal) runs over empty traces because there's no upstream trace-fetcher — see openQuestions[4]. Emits empty cooccurrence matrix; compose_goal handles defensively.

Signal 5 (cost_priors / risk_priors) does NOT iterate per producer candidate — see openQuestions[5]. Aggregated/placeholder lookups; compose_goal cross-references with forward_chain_producers_result's inline metrics.

Cycle detection inspects only the immediate parent's trace, not the full ancestor chain's trace tree — see openQuestions[6]. Conservative since depth guard (default 3) bounds recursion before deep cycles can form.
failure_mode JSON shape is enforced by the LLM prompt, not by schema validation — see openQuestions[7]. Update the prompt when migration 091's taxonomy evolves.
metadata.subscriberContract: Not a lifecycle subscriber. This activity is dispatched explicitly — typically by the impulse-binding-selection-layer slot-binding meta-activity when both pool selection and producer selection return unbindable=true, or directly by the workbench's spawn-subgoal affordance (sibling §4) when a missing-shape row in BackwardChainingPanel has no in-scope producer or only low-confidence producers.
metadata.guardSummary: Three recursion-safety guards (depth, cycle, budget) are embedded in the compose_goal LLM prompt. Each guard, when tripped, sets `human_in_the_loop_required: true` on the emitted goal impulse and populates `failure_mode` with the structured taxonomy from sibling validators-and-failure-modes (migration 091). The guards do NOT block emission — the goal emits in all cases — but the human gate flag instructs the downstream dispatcher to pause for review. Multi-guard tripping is supported via `failure_modes` array.
metadata.outputContract: Single goal-shaped impulse with body fields per design.md §Goal-as-shape-producer framing: text (LLM-composed), category='meta', target_shape, endpoint_output_shapes=[target_shape], available_shapes, depth=parent_depth+1, parent_execution_id, remaining_budget_usd, human_in_the_loop_required, failure_mode (or failure_modes array if multiple), signals_summary.
